messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT | routing.fallback.loop between us-east <-> us-west <-> eu detected. Traffic oscillating, ~15% errors on short requests, multiple health probes flapping. Auto-fallbacks engaged repeatedly. Alert fired: routing.pingflip.threshold exceeded.

sre_amy: ack. paging oncall now. @oncall-rotations-bot which rotation is live?

oncall-rotations-bot: Pager duty: @sre_amy is oncall for SRE today. Routing incident severity: P1. Paging: paged@sre_amy, paged@infra_mateo

sre_amy: I'm on it. quick snapshot — is this a misfire in health checks or an underlying host issue?

infra_mateo: seeing repeated health-check failures from regional routers. logs show probes returning 503s for short bursts (~10-30s) then recovered, then another region fails -> looks like fallback triggers cascade. stacktrace snippets:
```
router: probe->us-west returned 503 (model-init-timeout)
router: fallback to eu with variant v0.9-beta
router: eu probe then 504 -> fallback to us-east
```

ml_ops_li: suspicious — eu was getting rolled model-variant `v0.9-beta` overnight for canary. That variant has longer cold start on small instances (KV warmup). If routers treat slow init as unhealthy, they will route away and then the other region might hit the same variant and repeat.

platform_op_jess: confirmed we shipped a change to the fallback policy at 02:10 UTC — `max_failures=2, fallback_threshold_ms=150, prefer_lower_latency=true, allow_variant_fallback=true`. That `allow_variant_fallback=true` plus low threshold could be causing oscillation. I can temporarily disable variant fallback.

sre_amy: agreed mitigation plan: 1) stop variant fallback 2) increase probe timeouts to avoid marking slow inits as unhealthy 3) pin routing to last-known-good region for 15m. Who can apply 1 now?

platform_op_jess: I can flip variant fallback off. running command:
```
rbacctl patch routing policy-global --set allow_variant_fallback=false --reason "mitigate pingflip"
```

platform_op_jess: done. policy updated, propagation to routers in progress (:hourglass_flowing_sand:).

infra_mateo: pushing probe timeout bump: `probe_timeout_ms` 100 -> 450 on all regions. command queued:
```
infra-ctl rollout probes --regions us-east,us-west,eu --set probe_timeout_ms=450
```

infra_mateo: applied to control plane; agents report rollout started. will monitor.

prod_support_raj: customers reporting increased 5xxs on `/v1/generate` — preliminary impact: 12 customers flagged, mostly low-volume apps, estimated 6% of hosted requests affected in last 30m. I'm drafting an incident blurb for customer comms.

sre_amy: after policy flip, are we seeing the flap stop?

infra_mateo: metrics: routing oscillation count down from 42 -> 6 in 4m. error-rate trending down to normal. some routers still warming KV caches causing transient 503s but no full loop.

ml_ops_li: also paused canary rollout for `v0.9-beta` in eu/us-west. command:
```
modelctl abort-deploy --model v0.9-beta --regions eu,us-west
```

ml_ops_li: aborted. reverting instances that had `v0.9-beta` to `v0.8-stable` where possible.

platform_op_jess: pinned routing for 15min: `routing.pin.region=last-good` for affected prefixes. That prevents immediate cross-region fallbacks while caches warm. Command:
```
routingctl set pin-duration --prefix /v1/generate --duration 15m
```

sre_amy: good. Monitoring window open. infra, ml_ops, product support stay on thread until stable and then hand off to postmortem.

prod_support_raj: customer blurb draft:
"We experienced an intermittent routing fallback loop affecting some requests across regions (us-east, us-west, eu) between 02:09–02:45 UTC. Root cause: an aggressive fallback policy combined with a canary model variant with longer cold-starts. Impact: elevated 5xx errors for ~12 customers, roughly 6% of hosted requests for a short window. Mitigation: disabled variant fallback, increased probe timeouts, paused canary rollout, and pinned routing. We're continuing to monitor and will follow up with a postmortem and remediation plan."

sre_amy: timeline note: policy change 02:10 UTC, first oscillation 02:12, pager 02:14, mitigations applied 02:20–02:28, stable ~02:33. I'll set incident severity to mitigated and create a PMR.

platform_op_jess: opened a rollback PR for the policy change and flagged for review. Assigning to security/ops for policy testing before re-enable. PR: `github.com/redwood/routing/policies#2345`

ml_ops_li: follow-ups: add model warmup hooks for canary variants, ensure variant cold-start is not treated as health failure (suggest adding `initial_grace_period=120s` to probe logic), and tighter gating for `allow_variant_fallback`.

infra_mateo: follow-ups: add jitter to probe scheduling, make probe thresholds region-aware, and add a short cooldown after any fallback to prevent immediate re-fallback.

prod_support_raj: I'll send customer notifications and open support tickets for the 12 customers. Liaising with account teams now.

sre_amy: thanks team. I'll escalate to postmortem board and schedule a 1h RCA tomorrow. Leaving thread open while we confirm 30m stable window. please add logs/links if you find more details.

infra_mateo: adding link to live graphs: https://metrics.redwood.internal/d/route/oscillation?from=3629454000&to=3629462000

ml_ops_li: added model deploy logs: https://deploys.redwood.internal/logs/v0.9-beta

platform_op_jess: noting runbook ops: `RUNBOOK: routing-fallback-loop` updated with temporary steps.

sre_amy: incident status: mitigated, oncall remains until 03:05 UTC to verify. postmortem assigned: `PM-3629456789`. Closing live page once 30m clean.

incident-bot: Incident moved to status: mitigated by user sre_amy. Auto-notify scheduled for follow-up meeting.
